title: Microsoft Purview DLP: protect data sent to unmanaged cloud apps through the Island Enterprise Browser
summary: The briefing correctly reports the rollout, opt-in default and request-based billing. Hold it because the automation shown for auditing or blocking traffic only creates a policy, rather than configuring the rules that perform those actions. An older change note also attributes the rollout change to an unverified Microsoft notice.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview network data security is adding an Island integration.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview network data security now integrates with Island, extending protection to Island’s browser-based workflows at the point of user interaction.

claims.claim: Collection and DLP policies can detect and protect data shared with unmanaged cloud apps through Island Enterprise Browser, Island Extension and browser add-ins.
claims.quote: configure Microsoft Purview collection and data loss prevention policies to detect and protect data shared with unmanaged cloud apps through the Island Enterprise Browser, the Island Extension, and browser add ins via HTTP and HTTPS

claims.claim: The Island integration covers HTTP and HTTPS.
claims.quote: through the Island Enterprise Browser, the Island Extension, and browser add ins via HTTP and HTTPS

claims.claim: The integration uses the same classifiers, sensitive information types and sensitivity labels as other Purview policies.
claims.quote: using the same classifiers, sensitive information types, and sensitivity labels used in other Purview policies.

claims.claim: Island provides presentation-layer visibility and control over typed and pasted input, file transfers and extension activity.
claims.quote: Island provides visibility and control at the presentation layer, including typed and pasted input, file transfers, and extension activity, so data can be inspected before it ever leaves the browser.

claims.claim: The integration enriches DSPM and the IRM risk score and enables data security and compliance for AI interactions.
claims.quote: This integration further enriches Purview Data Security Posture Management (DSPM), Insider Risk Management (IRM) risk score, enables data security and compliance for AI interactions, and more.

claims.claim: There is no end-user impact unless administrators enable the integration and configure network data security policies.
claims.quote: There is no impact to end users unless administrators enable the integration and configure network data security policies in Purview.

claims.claim: Integrated solutions monitor network traffic and send data to Purview for classification and policy evaluation.
claims.quote: The integrated solutions monitor network traffic and send the data to Microsoft Purview for classification and policy evaluation.

claims.claim: Communication between the integrated solution and Purview is real-time for DLP protection.
claims.quote: When you apply protections via the use of DLP policies, the communication between the integrated solution and Microsoft Purview is in real time.

claims.quote: If you are using network data security for monitoring only via collection policies, the communication is asynchronous.

claims.claim: No Microsoft Learn automation is documented for enabling the Island Security Store integration.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Security Store Island integration enable PowerShell Microsoft Graph API; "Purview" "Security Store" "API" integration. Read dlp-create-policy-ai-network-data-security and Graph/Purview API search excerpts; no enablement operation found.

claims.claim: Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Inline web traffic reaches the entry to configuring network DLP.
claims.quote: Select Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy. Select Inline web traffic. Select Custom from the Categories list and then select Custom policy from the Regulations list.
claims.fix: The path is a correct entry point but stops before configuration. For the documented blocking scenario, extend it to 'Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Inline web traffic > Custom > Custom policy > + Add cloud apps > Adaptive app scopes > All unmanaged AI apps > Choose where to enforce the policy > Network and non-Microsoft secure browsers > Define policy settings > Create or customize advanced DLP rules > Customize advanced DLP rules > + Create rule > + Add an action > Restrict browser and network activities > Text sent to or shared with cloud or AI apps > Block'. Note that app/group selection and rule conditions must be completed for the intended policy, as described at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-create-policy-ai-network-data-security.

claims.claim: New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name <policy name> -EnforcementPlanes @("Network") is the automation counterpart for deciding which traffic is audited or blocked.
claims.quote: Use the New-DlpCompliancePolicy cmdlet to create data loss prevention (DLP) policies in the Microsoft Purview compliance portal. DLP policies contain DLP rules that identify, monitor, and protect sensitive information.
claims.fix: Change controls[1].governs and the matching rendered row label to 'Creation of network DLP policies', and change its note to 'General network data security policy creation, not Island-specific. Security & Compliance PowerShell; this command creates the policy container and does not configure traffic selection or Audit only/Block rules. Some features in the cited Learn scenario are in preview.' Keep the call: its syntax and Network value are documented, but its operation does not set the audit/block control currently claimed.

claims.claim: New-DlpCompliancePolicy is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: Some features used in the DLP network scenario are in preview.
claims.quote: Some features used in this scenario are in preview.

claims.claim: Data loss prevention > Classifiers > Collection policies > + Create policy reaches collection policy creation for network discovery.
claims.quote: Open the Data loss prevention solution and navigate to Classifiers > Collection policies. Select + Create policy.
claims.fix: The entry path is correct but stops before the collection settings. Extend the documented route to 'Data loss prevention > Classifiers > Collection policies > + Create policy > + Add condition > Content contains > Classifiers > Edit > + Add activities > + Add data source > Unmanaged cloud apps > Network and non-Microsoft secure browsers'. Note that classifier, activity, app and group choices are completed in that wizard, following https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/collection-policies-create-deploy-policy.
